text: Paul David Tonko (/ˈtɒŋkoʊ/ TONK-oh; born June 18, 1949) is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New York's 20th congressional district since 2013. He previously represented the 21st congressional district from 2009 to 2013. A member of the Democratic Party, Tonko is described as a staunch progressive. After the 2020 redistricting cycle, effective for the 118th Congress, the 20th district includes all of Albany, Saratoga, and Schenectady Counties as well as part of Rensselaer County. From 1983 to 2007, Tonko represented the 105th district in the New York State Assembly. He was appointed president and CEO of the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority in 2007 and resigned in April 2008. He subsequently declared his candidacy for Congress and was elected in November 2008. Tonko is the ranking member of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment in the 119th Congress and has held this position since 2013, making him the highest-ranking Democrat on the panel that authorizes, oversees, and investigates the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Tonko is a lifelong resident of Amsterdam, New York, near Schenectady, and is of primarily Polish descent. He graduated from Amsterdam's Wilbur H. Lynch High School in 1967 and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical and industrial engineering from Clarkson University in Potsdam, New York in 1971. As an engineer for the New York Public Service Commission, Tonko became active in local politics in the early 1970s and successfully ran for the Montgomery County Board of Supervisors. He served on the board from 1976 to 1983, serving as chairman from 1981 to 1983 and was the youngest person in county history to be elected to the board. In January 1983, Assemblywoman Gail S. Shaffer resigned her 105th district seat to become Secretary of State of New York. The Democratic and Liberal Parties nominated Tonko to run in a special April 12 election against Eugene Hallock, the Republican and Conservative nominee. Tonko defeated Hallock in a close race. He was reelected 13 times, serving in the Assembly until 2007. While in the Assembly, Tonko chaired the Energy Committee from 1992 until 2007 and was a member of standing committees on Agriculture, Transportation, and Education, where he was the original sponsor and chief proponent of the College Tuition Savings Program, signed into law in 1997. He sponsored Timothy's Law in 2006, which requires health insurers to cover mental health treatment, and the Northeast Dairy Compact. He also chaired the Legislative Commission on Rural Resources. Tonko resigned his Assembly seat in June 2007 to become president and CEO of the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority. On April 25, 2008, he stepped down from that position after ten-term Democratic Congressman Michael McNulty announced his retirement. He then entered the race to succeed McNulty in the 21st district, winning the Democratic primary on September 9, defeating four other candidates. In the November 4 general election, Tonko defeated Republican Schenectady County Legislator James Buhrmaster by a decisive margin. According to the Times Union, "Tonko's name recognition, accomplishment in the Legislature, such as the passage of mental health parity legislation, and his record" contributed to his win. The 21st district had long been the only safe Democratic district in the state outside New York City, Buffalo, and Rochester. Tonko ran for reelection on the Democratic, Working Families, and Independence Party lines, facing Republican and Conservative nominee Ted Danz, a former U.S. Navy Reservist and small business owner in the cooling and heating industry. Tonko raised almost $980,000 and spent almost $780,000 on his campaign, while Danz raised about $44,000 and spent about $42,000. The New York Times rated the seat "Solid Democratic" with a "99.8% to 100% chance" of Tonko winning. Major issues in the 2010 race included Tonko's votes for Obamacare, the Stimulus Package (ARRA), and the Energy Bill. The Albany Times Union endorsed Tonko, citing "a way of thinking and speaking like the engineer that he once was" and his support of the economic stimulus and health care bills. Tonko won the November 2 general election with 124,889 votes to 85,752. Redistricting renumbered Tonko's district as the 20th, which lost much of its rural territory to the west and was expanded into Saratoga County to compensate for population loss. The new 20th district remained no less Democratic than the old 21st. Tonko defeated Bob Dieterich in 2012, Jim Fischer in 2014, Joe Vitollo in 2016 and 2018, Liz Joy in 2020 and 2022, and Kevin Waltz in 2024. Tonko was one of the 19 most liberal House members according to the National Journal in 2011. He voted with President Joe Biden's stated position 100% of the time in the 117th Congress, according to a FiveThirtyEight analysis. When entering Congress, Tonko stated he wanted to focus on energy policy, the issue he said he knows best. He sponsored a bill to create an $800 million research program in wind energy technologies, which would benefit GE in his district, and sought to create a research program to improve the efficiency of gas turbines used in power generation systems. In 2010, he secured a provision in a House-passed bill, following the BP Gulf of Mexico disaster, to prevent future oil spills and support small businesses in spill research. In 2011, he sponsored an amendment to protect the Environmental Protection Agency's authority to regulate carbon emissions. Tonko praised the 2011 State of the Union address, calling it a bold agenda focused on growing the economy, jobs, and opportunity for the middle class. He has frequently warned about the threat that repealing Obamacare would pose to small businesses, young people, and seniors. Tonko has worked to raise awareness about the region's waterways, particularly the Hudson and Mohawk rivers and the effects of flooding after Hurricane Irene. To address these issues, he introduced the Hudson-Mohawk Basin Act in 2012. In 2015, Tonko became a prominent opponent of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), citing American trade deficits and the use of child labor by at least four countries that had already signed the pact as reasons for opposition. In 2017, Tonko was one of three Catholic politicians publicly rebuked by Bishop Edward Bernard Scharfenberger of Albany for participating in a rally supporting Planned Parenthood. In January 2019, Tonko, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, was named chair of its Subcommittee on the Environment and Climate Change. On October 1, 2020, Tonko co-signed a letter to Secretary of State Mike Pompeo condemning Azerbaijan’s offensive operations against the Armenian-populated enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh, denouncing Turkey’s role in the conflict, and criticizing "false equivalence between Armenia and Azerbaijan, even as the latter threatens war and refuses to agree to monitoring along the line of contact." In 2022, Tonko played a key role in passing provisions in the CHIPS and Science Act (PL 117-167) into law. In 2023, Tonko was among 56 Democrats to vote in favor of H. Con. Res. 21, which directed President Joe Biden to remove U.S. troops from Syria within 180 days. Tonko is a member of more than 65 House caucuses.
